          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: "User I/O" wait Class
Impact is 1.54 active sessions, 20.76% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
Waits for I/O to temporary tablespaces were not consuming significant database
time.
The throughput of the I/O subsystem was not significantly lower than expected.

   No recommendations are available.


Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is .94 active sessions, 12.66% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .94 active sessions, 12.66% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .83 active sessions, 11.16% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .49 active sessions, 6.67% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "5t2zax5wk7008".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 5t2zax5wk7008.
         INSERT INTO GLBKBPJ.TMPFDAYSTARTREP1(ACMASTCODE,AC_CODE,AC_NAME,MAC_N
         AME,AC_NO,GMST_CODE,NAME,MNAME,INST_DATE,
         AMOUNT,ADDR,MADDR,RTALUKA,MTALUKA,CITY,MCITY,
         PERIOD,P_UNIT,AC_STRT_DT,OPN_BAL,C_BAL,DEBIT,CREDIT) SELECT
         ACMASTCODE,AC_CODE,AC_NAME,MAC_NAME,AC_NO,GMST_CODE,NAME,MNAME,INST_D
         ATE, AMOUNT,ADDR,MADDR,RTALUKA,MTALUKA,CITY,MCITY,
         PERIOD,P_UNIT,AC_STRT_DT,OPN_BAL,C_BAL,DEBIT,CREDIT FROM (SELECT
         ACMASTCODE,AC_CODE,AC_NAME,MAC_NAME,AC_NO,GMST_CODE,NAME,MNAME,INST_D
         ATE,INST_AMT AS AMOUNT,ADDR,MADDR,RTALUKA,MTALUKA,CITY,MCITY,
         PERIOD,P_UNIT,AC_STRT_DT,OPN_BAL,C_BAL,DEBIT,CREDIT
         FROM
         (
         SELECT A.ACMASTCODE,A.AC_CODE,A.AC_NAME,A.MAC_NAME,L.AC_NO,L.GMST_COD
         E,K.NAME,K.MNAME,L.AC_DUE_DT,
         NVL(L.INST_AMT,:"SYS_B_00") INST_AMT,B.PEND_INST PEND_AMT,
         ADD_MONTHS(L.INST_DATE,C.SRNO*NVL(L.INST_PRD,:"SYS_B_01"))  AS
         INST_DATE,K.ADDR,K.MADDR,
         K.RTALUKA,K.MTALUKA,K.CITY,K.MCITY,L.PERIOD,L.P_UNIT,L.AC_STRT_DT,L.O
         PN_BAL,L.C_BAL,L.DEBIT,L.CREDIT,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY L.ACMASTCODE,L.AC_NO ORDER BY C.SRNO DESC)
         AS RNO
         FROM ACMAST A ,LNMAS L,LNACCINTMAS B,(SELECT LEVEL AS SRNO FROM DUAL
         CONNECT BY LEVEL<=:"SYS_B_02") C,BANKMAS K
         WHERE A.SUB_TYPE = :"SYS_B_03"
         AND A.AC_TYPE = :"SYS_B_04"
         AND A.ACMASTCODE = L.ACMASTCODE
         AND L.ACMASTCODE = B.ACMASTCODE
         AND L.AC_NO = B.AC_NO
         AND L.GMST_CODE = K.GMST_CODE
         AND NVL(L.POST,:"SYS_B_05") = :"SYS_B_06"
         AND NVL(L.CLOSED,:"SYS_B_07") = :"SYS_B_08"
         AND NVL(B.PEND_INST,:"SYS_B_09") > :"SYS_B_10"
         AND ADD_MONTHS(L.INST_DATE,C.SRNO*NVL(L.INST_PRD,:"SYS_B_11"))
         BETWEEN  :"SYS_B_12" AND :"SYS_B_13"
         )
         WHERE RNO=:"SYS_B_14" )

Finding 4: Soft Parse
Impact is .69 active sessions, 9.29% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .69 active sessions, 9.29% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .69 active sessions, 9.29% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .49 active sessions, 6.67% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .49 active sessions, 6.67% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .98 active sessions, 13.23% of total activity.


Finding 6: Undersized SGA
Impact is .38 active sessions, 5.12% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
